scientificAndNumericalReview: The exact proposal matches the proposal embedded in input.json. Its elementary calculations are correct: phase accelerations are 1.333… m/s², 0 and −2.0 m/s²; interval accelerations are 1.6, 1.6 and 0.8 m/s²; trapezoid distances are 3.2, 9.6, 14.4, 16.0 and 12.0 m, totaling 55.2 m. The first acceleration sequence is nonincreasing, rather than strictly decreasing. Independently, t_F=0.5048187773 s and x=4.0385502188 m, correctly reported as 0.505 s and 4.04 m. The measured mean is 2.99 m, its nominal shortfall is 1.0485502188 m, or 25.96%, and 0.13 m is the full observed spread, not a ± deviation about the mean. The principal defects concern the physical meaning of the comparison, unsupported causal and quantitative conclusions, and the carry-forward exception. Correct arithmetic does not establish the key’s explanation.
partOneToThreePreservationReview: DE and EN task statements 1–3, their solutions and s1–s3 are genuinely unchanged. The same is true of task 4, its solution and s4; materials 1–3 are also unchanged. The 13 changed fields concern the two descriptions, coverage, strands, review metadata, total/pass points, scoring steps, and both languages’ task and solution texts. Material 4, the surrounding context and global marking notes materially alter the assessment despite preservation of the old numbered passages. The maxima change from (7,6,7,6,4) to (7,6,7,6,10). Parts 1–3 retain 20 available points, but their share falls from 66.67% to 55.56%; parts 1–4 fall from 86.67% to 72.22%. The pass mark rises from 60% to 77.78%. Thus unchanged old answers do not imply unchanged whole-assessment meaning.
partFourIntervalAndComparisonReview: Using the stipulated positive-input minimum/maximum calculation gives x_min=3.7035864633 m and x_max=4.3855139742 m. Outward rounding to [3.70,4.39] m is correct; the unrounded width is 0.6819275109 m. The observed uncertainty intervals are [2.93,3.03], [3.01,3.11] and [2.88,2.98] m. All are disjoint from the prediction; the nearest gap is 0.5935864633 m, or 0.59 m using the displayed lower bound. This establishes incompatibility of the stipulated prediction with those data and uncertainty bounds, conditional on matching the predicted and measured observable. It does not identify a unique cause. The interval is a rectangular uncertainty envelope, not a statistical confidence interval. No actual trial flight times, distributions or correlations are supplied. Material 3’s flight-time uncertainty must not be treated as evidence that the trials actually had the model’s nominal fall time. The unchanged part-4 calculation now controls mandatory K4, making its carry-forward treatment consequential.
pointParticleAndRotationObservableReview: Material 4 measures the horizontal coordinate of S relative to the ramp edge when any part of the car first contacts the ground. It does not measure the front’s landing coordinate or the displacement until S has fallen exactly 1.25 m. The calculation assumes a point released at the edge, zero vertical initial velocity, and a specified vertical drop. Edge height alone does not establish the COM release height or its drop to first contact. Equal launch/contact clearance could make that drop equal to the edge height, but the necessary geometry is not established. In uniform gravity, rotation does not itself invalidate ballistic COM motion; it changes body geometry and the contact event. K2’s fixed-orientation condition describes translation, but alone neither establishes simultaneous wheel contact nor the asserted COM drop, and it is unnecessary for predicting the COM trajectory itself. The nominal wheelbase traversal time is 2.6/8=0.325 s, or 0.644 times t_F. It does not determine actual support duration during pitching, release position, vertical release velocity, pitch angle, angular velocity or contact time. A forward COM release offset must also enter a coordinate measured from the edge. Forward tipping is plausible, but front-first contact does not establish when it began or a necessary metre-scale shortening. COM height, contact-point geometry, overhang distribution, suspension behavior and angular dynamics are insufficiently specified. Material 4’s horizontal-departure wording also needs reconciliation with the key’s downward COM velocity at release. The mandatory claim of several decimetres to approximately 1 m is underdetermined.
airResistanceBoundReview: Under the nominal point-release and fixed-drop assumptions, the direct translational estimates have the correct scale. The horizontal fixed-time bound is 0.02548420 m. Upward vertical resistance bounded by 0.2 m/s² gives t_max=sqrt(2.5/9.61)=0.510044784 s, an increase of 0.005226007 s and a horizontal increase of 0.04180805 m. Thus approximately −0.03 to +0.04 m is reasonable as a rounded estimate, but +0.04 m is not a strict outward upper bound. The small ratio 0.2/g=0.02039 supports the nominal-time scale estimate. The signs require horizontal retardation and upward resistance during downward motion; the unsigned acceleration bound alone does not supply them. Allowing either component sign gives a conservative point-model range change of approximately [−0.06552,+0.06782] m, still much smaller than the discrepancy. A few centimetres is small against the interval width and metre-scale shortfall, but comparable to the individual ±0.05 m measurement uncertainty. More seriously, the supplied acceleration bound controls translation, not aerodynamic torque or orientation-mediated contact-time changes. It therefore cannot establish the claimed centimetre bound for the actual first-contact observable or exclude every aerodynamic contribution to pitching.
passBoundaryAndMissingCoreReview: Let q=s1+s2+s3+s4, with q≤26. The authored s5 levels are 0 for no correct contribution; 1 for some but incomplete core performance; 7 for all K1–K5; and 8, 9 or 10 when one, two or three independent V additions are also earned. Scores 2–6 are not authored levels, and additions count only after the core level. Old s5=0/1/2/3/4 required q≥18/17/16/15/14. New s5=0 or 1 cannot pass, with maxima 26 and 27; s5=7/8/9/10 requires q≥21/20/19/18. Fractional scores in s1–s4 cannot breach the 27 ceiling when a core is missing. No additional required-step field is needed for that mathematical result. Missing s1/s2/s3/s4/s5 gives old total maxima 23/24/23/24/26 and new maxima 29/30/29/30/26. Any one old task can therefore still be absent in a passing new result. Across passes, s1–s3 can total as little as 12/20 now, versus 8/20 previously. All V additions may be absent: 26+7=33 passes, so the gate does not protect every quantitative demand in task 5c. Genuine failure of any authored core blocks passing, but K1 permits naming supplied assumptions; K2 and K3 explicitly require independent justification. Scientifically defective K2/K3/K5 interpretations accepted by the key can nevertheless count as complete. Carry-forward presents a further conflict: full s1–s3 gives 20; an arithmetic-error interval [2.70,4.39] m can receive s4=0 yet contain all measured intervals. A learner can consistently conclude compatibility, supply the other cores including a possible explanation of the nominal shortfall, and earn V1, giving 20+0+8=28 under the explicit carry-forward exception. Literal K4 instead requires incompatibility and would block this route. The proposal does not resolve that precedence conflict, so false compatibility is an admissible passing interpretation, not a guaranteed outcome under every grading interpretation.
MODWholeGoalCoverageReview: The current MOD goal requires justification of motion-model idealizations and identification of prediction limits. Task 5 intends to elicit this through point-particle justification, a drag estimate, comparison and diagnosis; K2/K3 appropriately reject merely copied assumptions. This is more substantial than naming supplied assumptions. Nevertheless, exact whole-MOD coverage is not defensible: mandatory criteria endorse an insufficient point-particle condition and an underdetermined causal diagnosis, the drag bound is extended beyond its established observable, and carry-forward can protect a false compatibility conclusion. Some quantitative demands are optional additions rather than pass-protected core performances. Prerequisite use supplies preparation, not direct graded coverage. Stunt planning or an optional proposed adjustment is planning evidence, and supplied trial data are not evidence that this learner performed an experiment. The exact file should therefore receive no whole-MOD credit pending correction.
fullPreparationAndSourceStageReview: Recursive traversal of the two declared prerequisites reaches exactly all 72 supplied context goals: 15 Physics and 57 Mathematics, with no missing or extraneous supplied nodes. This complete closure prepares graph interpretation, signed rates, areas, motion laws, free fall, horizontal projection, uncertainty notation, error classification and qualitative air-resistance/model reasoning. It contains no substantive preparation in support-force/tipping dynamics or quantitative first-contact geometry. Those omissions matter because the exact task requires a causal and order-of-magnitude diagnosis, not because a general rotation course would be desirable. Additional prerequisites cannot supply absent physical data. Official Physics printed p30 supports E.1 idealization through neglect of rotation/extension and friction, together with motion laws and experimental free fall. Horizontal projection is listed under E.3 on p31; Newtonian mechanics under E.2 and rotational topics under E.7 are distinct content. E.1 is a topic code within E1/E2 mechanics, not proof of first-semester placement or an official separate E1 LK requirement. An own voluntary offer for prospective LK learners can deepen E.1 using the already declared projectile preparation. The exact unsupported diagnosis is not justified by that designation. No entire E.2/E.7, aerodynamics or advanced uncertainty course is required for the sound kinematic and acceleration-bound work.

Rotation necessarily changes the COM’s ballistic trajectory in uniform gravity.
The nominal wheelbase traversal time establishes actual support duration, pitch evolution or a shortening of several decimetres to approximately 1 m.
Front-first touchdown establishes that pitching began during the rear-supported transition and uniquely explains the measured discrepancy.
Downward release velocity and front-first contact establish the net shortening of a COM coordinate measured from the edge without accounting for release position and geometry.
A translational acceleration bound establishes a centimetre bound on orientation-dependent first-contact range or excludes all aerodynamic causes.
Three consistently low measurements identify a particular systematic measurement error or unique physical mechanism.
The verbal completeness claim and numerical core gate guarantee scientifically valid whole-MOD attainment despite the key and carry-forward conflicts.
